lyrics:
[Intro: live drums, upright bass, pizzicato strings]

[Chorus: female neo-soul voice, calm and warm]
Text when you land, call when you're in
I'll leave the light on low
Different time zones, same old house
Baby, I got us, you know
I got us

[Verse 1: male rap, relaxed, a little tired]
Mile marker ninety, coffee's gone cold
Eighteen wheels and a podcast getting old
You're clocking in right when I'm pulling off the road
We high-five in the driveway, that's the code
Folks at the diner asking how we make it work
I say she's got my back and I got hers
Friday I'm home and the kids got a game
I'll be the loud one yelling your last name

[Chorus: female neo-soul voice, calm and warm]
Text when you land, call when you're in
I'll leave the light on low
Different time zones, same old house
Baby, I got us, you know
I got us

[Verse 2: female rap, quick and sure]
Third floor, night shift, charts in my hand
Lady in bed nine asking 'bout my man
I say he's somewhere outside Tulsa, eating bad
She says, "You trust him?" I say, "Ma'am, he's all I've had."
Your mother thinks I'm crazy, mine thinks you're gone
They ain't in the group chat, they don't know what's going on
Lunch at three a.m., I send a picture of my tray
You send a sunrise back. That's the whole day.

[Bridge: strings swell, both voices trading]
Miss you. (Miss you more.)
Eat something. (You first.)
Lock the door. (It's locked.)
Love you. (I know. Drive.)

[Final Chorus: female voice, harmonies, drums double-time]
Text when you land, call when you're in
I'll leave the light on low
Different time zones, same old house
Baby, I got us, you know
I got us

[Outro: fast breakbeat ending, strings racing, a message chime]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 82 BPM, 4/4, C minor, with a fast double-time drum break at the very end. Warm, live and intimate.

VOICE: A man raps verse 1 in a relaxed, weary, good-humoured voice. A woman raps verse 2 quickly and confidently. A second woman sings the chorus in a calm, warm, slightly nasal neo-soul voice with jazz phrasing. The two rappers trade short lines in the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A live drum kit played with a tight, dry sound, an upright bass, pizzicato and bowed strings, an electric piano, a muted guitar, and in the outro a fast live breakbeat with racing strings.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, drums and bass. 0:14 Chorus 1. 0:42 Verse 1. 1:28 Chorus 2. 1:56 Verse 2. 2:42 Bridge. 3:00 Final chorus. 3:28 Outro, fast breakbeat, a chime at 3:56.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1990s Philadelphia live hip-hop: organic, warm and dry, a real band in a room, voices close.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'You send a sunrise back. That's the whole day.' at 2:36.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a musician on tour and his worried girlfriend. This is a trucker and a night nurse, married twenty years, for whom the reassurance has become routine and is no less real.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Apart, steady, teased by doubters, sure.
